title: 8.4 family — full-metric cross-engine
subtitle: MyVector 8.4 · vsql_vector (VillageSQL 8.4) · pgvector · MariaDB — fashion-mnist-784
nav: 9.7 family → · real-dataset (MySQL versions) · village (recall/QPS) · cross-engine
description: Controlled same-host 4-way, re-run 2026-11-10: current-main MyVector (MySQL 8.4, PR #278 + #280) vs vsql_vector, pgvector (Postgres 17) and MariaDB 12.3 — all on one A1 host, each pinned to the same cores with its working set cached above the ~188 MB index, run one-at-a-time, on fashion-mnist-784 vs published ground truth. At matched recall@10 MyVector leads ~2–3×. The pgvector/vsql/MariaDB baselines are the same controlled measurements as the /fair/ page — only MyVector’s MySQL version differs here.
caveats: Fresh controlled re-run (2026-11-10) — supersedes the earlier numbers on this page, which showed MyVector’s scalar build (pre-#278, recall 0.934 at ef=10) measured under host load. Now: current main (#278 vectorized kernels + keepPrunedConnections, #280 ANN-rewrite overhead removed), all engines pinned to the same cores, each cache-sized above the index, run sequentially.

The honest read (matched recall@10): MyVector (MySQL 8.4) serves the most QPS at every matched-recall point (~2.7k vs pgvector ~1.3k / vsql ~1.2k at recall 0.975). The old “MyVector trails” was the scalar, pre-#280 build under load; #278 fixed recall-per-ef and #280 removed the per-query overhead. Residual engine overhead (JSON_TABLE round-trip) is designed out in RFC-006.

Cache parity: MyVector holds its HNSW graph in its own memory; pgvector shared_buffers=2 GB; vsql InnoDB pool 4 GB; MariaDB InnoDB pool 2 GB + mhnsw_max_cache_size=1 GiB. All pinned to cores 12–15 and run one-at-a-time.

Dataset / params: fashion-mnist-784-euclidean (60k×784, L2), HNSW M=16, ef_construction=200 (MariaDB fixes it at 10). Recall@10 vs published neighbors. 500 queries/point; headline cards = warm ef_search=200.

Honest limits: same-host run on a shared A1 box (controlled via core-pinning + cache-parity + sequential runs, not a dedicated quiet machine); each engine uses its own server-side-timed harness. Method disclosed — read ~2–3× as ‘clearly ahead’, not a precise ratio.
